title: Apartheid imprisonment on Robben Island
summary: Robben Island’s maximum-security prison held political prisoners under apartheid. The buildings from this period now document confinement, resistance and the struggle against racial oppression in South Africa.

claims.text: Robben Island’s maximum-security prison held political prisoners under apartheid. The buildings from this period now document confinement, resistance and the struggle against racial oppression in South Africa.
Source specifies the 1960s through the 1990s; endpoints are coarse, not exact opening and closure dates.

The prison is one part of a much longer island history. Reading its material remains alongside the transition to inclusive elections helps distinguish experiences of imprisonment from the later commemoration of democracy.
